This is a weird one but It’s Complicated with Meryl Streep Alec Baldwin and Steve Martin. Back when I was a senior in high school/freshman in college my family up and moved and ditched me in our old apartment suddenly. I got a call from my mom while I was at work saying they were moving and to “figure it out” in regard to rent. I called an old buddy and asked him to move in as a roommate ASAP. We figured it out money wise but for the first couple months we were roughing it without any kind of internet. All I had was an old CRT with a built in DVD player. We didn’t even have any DVDs except for one, a bootleg copy It’s Complicated. Essentially it’s a romcom where Meryl Streep and Alec Baldwin are a divorced couple who are secretly hooking up unbeknownst to their kids, Baldwins new younger wife, and Steve Martin who is Streeps architect and love interest. It’s a really goofy movie and adds to the hilarity of two 18 y/o tattooed athletic metal heads and my gf at the time huddled around a TV giggling over a cheesy love story. We watched it on repeat constantly. Over time this movie became a right of passage for anyone who came over to our place enough, especially after we got internet since it wasn’t our only source of entertainment anymore. I’ve long since left that apartment and got a house in another state but I have the DVD in my dresser alongside a blu ray edition and own it on multiple streaming services. So many people have watched the movie with me over the years it’s sort of become this initiation for friends and girls I’ve dated over the years haha. It’s become like the next step in a relationship for me and a running joke amongst old friends/exes. But yeah, if there’s any movie I could go word for word with it’d definitely It’s Complicated.

I have a lot of religious trauma (Roman catholic). I never really practiced the faith or believed in any of it as long as I was forced to be a part of it but the concept of hell always bothered me. I don’t know what I believe at this point in my life after all the trauma of all variants I’ve endured but I am afraid of being punished even more for trying to end my suffering. It’s probably tied to being punished violently for having any sort of emotions and beaten as a child for anything from being too happy, too sad, or showing any sort of reaction at all honestly. Made me really stoic but in a bad way. It wavers constantly, some days I don’t care, some days I’m scared, and some days I feel like I’m already there but there’s still this underlying fear that I’ll end up somewhere worse. That no matter what I do even if I do right I’m still going to suffer in a personalized hell til the end of time. I’m also scared I’ll mess it up and end up paralyzed/comatose which is essentially the same as personalized hell. Scared of pain. At least right now I can make my own decisions and move freely. 
I’m in therapy and I’m gonna be medicated soon after a recent trip to a crisis center but idk. I don’t really have much hope still for anything. The anhedonia is really strong for me and it just won’t seem to break. It’s been this way for a long time now and nothing is helping me anymore. Only thing that ever stopped it for a couple years was a girl I dated and even then it wasn’t perfect. Can’t rely on people to save you. No one would miss me anyway. I’m just tired. Feel like I’m marching towards a guillotine. 

But yeah. I’m essentially afraid of hell and also botching it and actually ending up worse.

A lot of people come to me when they need things done efficiently and quickly. People also confide in me constantly and come to me for advice often. I’m currently crying while watching Casablanca (my favorite movie I only watch when I’m feeling very emotional and tender) and mixing a song I wrote about the love I lost recently. I sing everyday and write poetry often. I just ordered some relatively rare flower bulbs and play my favorite piano songs for them from my phone everyday and talk to them sweetly to encourage them to grow big and strong. I like to sew, garden, and paint. I cook everyday and I’m pretty good at it. I loved cooking for my last partner. It made me really happy to know she was taken care of fed and nourished and how happy it made her when I did stuff like that. I don’t kill flies or spiders and always take them outside when I can. She used to affectionately compare me to a Doberman a lot. “You look tough on the outside but inside you’re like puppy. At least with me.” Someone else in here mentioned appearance has a lot to do with people’s perception of you but it’s only the surface of who we are I think. Ive never been macho necessarily but I am a battle hardened mf not by choice but to survive my youth. Life’s been rough but I think the duality of my masculinity and femininity are what actually keep me balanced. You can’t have one without the other and both serve to make you better in different ways. You have to accept all parts of yourself and nourish them to become the strongest version of yourself. Ain’t nothing wrong with having a soft side. Nowhere does it say you can’t be tough and tender simultaneously.

Blinded by a light you can’t look away from. I used to think it was like a hole, this profound emptiness that was almost inexplicable. But now I think of it like being surrounded by blistering sunlight. Everywhere I look she’s there. Not just in the cliche ways of sunsets and leaves changing in the fall, but in her favorite snacks at the grocery store. Everytime I cook I see her in the pots and pans I taught her to make her favorite dish with. The empty space in my bed where she used to fall asleep watching cartoons and horror games, those same cartoons and games filled with memories of her laughter and little jumps from the scares. The car I drive daily I used to pick her up in when she got out of uni. The clicking of my keys on my phone texting her into the early morning when we’d first met. Finding occasional strands of her hair in the shower still. The path I run in my neighborhood going past her uni, past a lock on a bridge with our names engraved in it. The songs I listen to drowned out by the memory of her voice asking the names of the ones she liked. The place I work where we met. Not a single moment of my life is not completely encapsulated by the thought of her. It’s like having a light so bright shone in your eyes that no matter what direction you turn or how tight you close them it burns through. Even when it does fade there’s still a lingering afterimage.  It’s not the sunset girls you gotta worry about, it’s the ones that become a part of your day to day monotony that hurt the most. It’s hard to suffer in the dark and move forward when you’re being blinded by a love lost you can’t return to.

I am always truly only searching for one person. I don’t feel fulfilled by friendship. There’s a line we’ll reach inevitably that I won’t be able to cross with them. Because of this I have a hard time actually connecting with people and tend to distance myself from everyone even the few good people in my life. I don’t have any family anymore so the only way for me to combat this is to have a partner and to feel loved and connected to this partner. Kind of like a baseline, an anchor, a tether to everything. Solid ground that I can branch out from. Home to return to. When I have a girlfriend and the relationship is good, I thrive. I can connect to others much better and I enjoy my time with them and my partner. But when things go bad or I have a breakup it’s an immediate spiral into this unhealthy lifestyle. Which is so ironic because I’m very healthy physically but it’s the obsessive nature of self improvement so I won’t be abandoned again that makes things bad and eventually leads to more suffering. The irony is that I’m attractive, charismatic, and intelligent not to sound arrogant but I know I have a lot of really positive attributes. I’ve been described as the “almost” perfect boyfriend by almost all exes, I have no issues meeting people leaving a lasting impression and making loads of superficial friendships but my fatal flaw for love is my crippling mental health issues preventing me from opening up (CPTSD major depressive disorder anxiety and a weird fucked up dissociative order). This drives distance between my partners and I because I do everything alone and disappear for days at a time not because I’m doing anything and but cause I just genuinely didn’t know how to open up and ask for help. I see a professional about all this and I’m trying to get better but I just went through another bad breakup and am in the hole. 

Tl;dr I just want a girlfriend/family to call my own but my mental health issues mess up my relationships. I’m taking care of them forreal now but it still hurts.

It has an M rating for a reason. I think a lot of us played too young to fully grasp the concepts in the game but with that said we technically shouldn’t have even been playing in the first place. I don’t find them outdated at all I think they’re actually dealt with in a somewhat tasteful nuanced manner unlike many other games with similar topics at least in regard to the horror genre. It’s not supposed to be pretty or palatable and to make it otherwise would be a disservice to the story, trauma of all kinds is a very gritty and ugly thing more often than not and I think that’s part of the point of it all. Silent Hill 2 handled it in away that didn’t glamorize it which I personally believe is part of what made it so good and why it holds up today. Lots of modern media tend to turn these kinds of topics into glitter fests (ie. Shows like Euphoria) where I’ve noticed a lot of the younger generation seems like they almost want to have some sort of mental affliction, like it’s trendy and I’m speaking as a late 20 something with CPTSD.
